### ⚠️ Identity finding — this is the round's most useful output, and it is why the seat is standing down

`get_me` returns **`yinlianghui`**, the maintainer's own account. Chasing that down produced a measured map of **three distinct identities** on four channels, which no prior brief records:

| channel | authenticates as | objectui | objectstack |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| MCP GitHub tools (issues/labels/PRs) | **`yinlianghui`** | ✅ writes confirmed | unverified |
| `git push` (`GH_TOKEN`) | **`yinlianghui-tw`** | ✅ push OK (dry-run) | ❌ **403** |
| raw REST via `curl` | `yinlianghui-tw` | ❌ **403** | ❌ 403 |
| commit author | `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>` | — | — |

Two things this settles that were previously guesses:

1. **The "403 via the proxy" this seat recorded for ref deletion is not a permission scope — it is the proxy refusing direct `api.github.com` outright**: `{"message":"GitHub access is not enabled for this session. An org admin must connect the Claude GitHub App for this organization."}`. Every GitHub read/write must go through the MCP tools. A seat that reasons "I got a 403, so I lack that permission" will draw the wrong conclusion.
2. **`git push` to `objectstack` is denied for agent seats in this session shape** (`Claude doesn't have GitHub access to objectstack-ai/objectstack for your organization`), while `objectui` push works. Cross-repo work must be filed via MCP issue tools, ⛔ never assumed pushable.

⚠️ **While the seat runs under `yinlianghui`, every claim lands with the maintainer as assignee.** A future seat must ⛔ **not** read those as the #4806 "non-loop identity, never touch" case. The `Session:` line is the arbiter. The maintainer is changing the bound account, so the next seat should re-run `get_me` rather than inherit this.

R5 landed nothing, so it cost nothing this round — but it blocks the first PR of the next round.

### Work fully prepared and left on the cards, ⛔ not lost

R5's verification survives the stand-down; the next seat should **reuse rather than re-derive**. Three candidates were selected and premise-checked against `origin/main` @ `e52fac0`:

1. **#4820 + #5380 — FOLD.** Both ratchet lists (`KNOWN_MISSING_TARGETS`, `KNOWN_MISSING_PACKAGE_ALIAS_TARGETS:804`) are in the **same file**, so serialising pays the rebase tax twice for two three-line edits. Full fold rationale, five-gate check, per-card acceptance criteria and the ⛔ exclusion list are on #4820. Both forks already adjudicated to **direction A** — ⛔ do not re-open.
2. **#5174 batch 2.** Scope taken from the R4 comment, ⛔ not the body. Suggested batch: `plugins` 20 · `building-crud-app` 21 · `rfcs/0001-clipboard-paste` 23 · `architecture` 25 = **89 diagnostics / 4 pages**, matching batch 1's proven throughput (90). Leaves `plugin-development` 25 · `schema-rendering` 27 · `theming` 29 for batch 3, and `layout` 45 + `component-registry` 59 for a batch of their own. Read-coupling to #4820 was measured and **ruled out** (0 hits for either specifier across all nine pages; positive control 12).
3. **#5408 — premise settled by the PM, not deferred to the dev.** The card's own blocker was *"cannot be settled from inside the checkout — needs the repository's Security settings."* It can: `list_workflows` returns **31** workflows with **four** `dynamic/*` entries (Copilot ×2, Dependabot, Claude) and **no `dynamic/github-code-scanning/codeql`**. CodeQL default setup is **off**, so case 1 holds — the badge is false and should go. The four dynamic entries are the positive control that the listing does surface dynamic workflows. ⛔ Adding a CodeQL workflow is a separate question, not a rider. Note the repo *does* have `Secret Scanning` (`.github/workflows/secret-scan.yml`) — ⛔ do not report it as having no security scanning at all.

### Method note worth keeping

**The decision re-read paid for itself twice in one round.** #4820 and #5380 both *read* like open A/B forks — both bodies say the choice is the maintainer's, and #4820's own guard docblock says so in code. Both had in fact been adjudicated to direction A in triage comments days earlier. Dispatching from the bodies, or escalating to the maintainer, would have re-opened two settled rulings. ⛔ The card body is not the ruling; the comments are.

Post-merge re-verification on `origin/main` with a positive control (`layout.md` still in the ledger = 1, proving the grep works): CodeQL badge 0 · dead paths 0 · ratchet `= []` · the four ledger entries 0.

### ⚠️ The round's most important output is a CORRECTION, not a landing

**Three consecutive seats — including this one — recorded that objectui's PRs bypass the merge queue. That is false, and it was falsified by attempting the action rather than inspecting metadata.**

| # | reading | result |
|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `PUT …/pulls/5963/merge` | **405 — "Changes must be made through the merge queue"** |
| 2 | `enable_pr_auto_merge`, all checks green | merged 09:43:27Z |
| 3 | repo-wide `event=merge_group` runs, **after** that merge | **0** |
| 4 | positive control, `event=pull_request` on `ci.yml` | **4,978** |
| 5 | workflows declaring `merge_group` on `main` | **8** (`ci`, `lint`, `changeset-presence`, `control-bytes`, `doc-component-types`, `doc-snippet-types`, `docs-links`, `skills-paths`) |

**Reading 1 alone kills "seats bypass the queue" — bypass is not available to anyone.** Auto-merge *is* the ruleset-sanctioned path here, so ⛔ no seat ever violated 「永不队列外 auto-merge」, and ⛔ no skill exception is needed.

**Readings 1+3+5 give the real, worse finding:** the queue is enforced and merges **without validating anything**. #3523's step 2 landed (the `merge_group` triggers exist in eight files); its step 3 — making those checks *required in the queue* — did not. That is **#4986**, still open and still accurate.

⚠️ **The specific error to not repeat:** two seats, then I, read `merged_by: <a human-shaped account>` as evidence of bypass. **It is not — GitHub attributes a queue merge to whoever enqueued it.** I wrote "verified this round rather than inherited" while having verified the wrong thing, in a card complaining that other seats propagated unverified claims. Filed and then **rewritten** as **objectstack#11621**, with the retraction preserved as its first comment.

### #5380 — `pm:retriage`, ⛔ not implemented

Dispatched folded with #4820; its premise-first stop condition fired and the dev correctly stopped. `packages/runner/src/app-data` is **not a dead target** — it is a documented, deliberately git-ignored, **user-supplied** directory (`.gitignore:1`, `README.md:85` and `content/docs/utilities/runner.mdx:156` both say *symlink*, `MetadataLoader.ts:19-28` reads it). That falsifies the grounds of **both** ruled directions: A inherited #3593, whose target was a *deleted package*; B claims the docs are missing, and they exist.

Card is `pm:queue` + `pm:retriage`, dissent recorded, claim released. ⛔ This seat did not re-adjudicate. Consequence filed as **#5968** (#5168's pin is checkout-state dependent — following the runner README's step 1 turns it red on the developer's own machine; green in CI only because CI never creates the directory).

## ⚠️ Operational finding — **`mergeable_state: "behind"` silently keeps an armed, fully green PR out of the merge queue**

Recorded by the `domain:devx` @ objectui execution seat, PM session `session_019b5UBNMtTzKbVtZZGvFuxe`, 2026-08-25 ~00:30Z. This one cost 40 minutes and I nearly explained it away.

### What happened

PR **#6189** (card #5867 batch 5) was armed at 23:49Z: `draft: false`, auto-merge SQUASH enabled, **all checks green**, combined status `success`. Forty minutes later it had not merged, while PRs armed both **before** it (#6187, #6191, #6192, #6193) and **after** it (#6195, #6196) had merged or were building.

### ⛔ My first explanation was wrong, and I had already said it out loud

I reasoned that three PRs armed within 25 minutes, each needing its own 10–15 minute queue build, explained a serial backlog — and concluded *"nothing is wrong, I won't probe it destructively."* That was a plausible story fitted to the symptom, and it was **false**.

### The read-only probe that settled it

⭐ `list_workflow_runs` on `ci.yml` filtered to **`event: merge_group`** lists every queue build by its `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-NNNN-*` branch. That is decisive and costs nothing:

```
00:22:27  in_progress   gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-6196-…
00:17:54  in_progress   gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-6195-…
00:00:01  completed ✓   gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-6191-…
23:57:25  completed ✓   gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-6193-…
…
```

**#6189 appears nowhere in that list.** It never entered the queue at all — so "serial backlog" was refuted by the absence of the thing a backlog would have produced.

`pull_request_read` then gave the cause: **`mergeable_state: "behind"`**. Its base is `670f5732`; `main` had moved to `17ccec977`, four commits ahead. The PRs that merged were all created against a newer base.

### Why this is worth a seat-level note

⚠️ **"Behind" is invisible in every place a PM normally looks.** The PR is not draft. Auto-merge is armed. Every check is green. Combined status is `success`. There is no red, no conflict banner in the API payload, no failed step — the PR simply sits, and the standing rule *"armed + clean + unmerged is NORMAL for a merge queue"* is exactly wrong here while looking exactly right.

⛔ The `405 Pull Request is in the merge queue` probe would **not** have caught this either: it distinguishes "in the queue" from "arm failed", and this is a third state — armed, not in the queue, not failed.

### The remedy, and the rule going forward

`update_pull_request_branch` on #6189 (merge `main` in — ⛔ never a rebase or force-push on a branch someone else may have checked out). CI re-runs, then the queue takes it.

**New standing check for this seat**: when an armed, green PR has not merged within ~20 minutes, do **not** attribute it to queue contention. Read two things:

1. `mergeable_state` — `behind` means update the branch; `blocked` / `dirty` mean something else again.
2. `list_workflow_runs` with `event: merge_group` — if there is no `gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-NNNN-*` run, it is **not in the queue**, whatever the arm said.

⭐ The general lesson is the one this lane keeps re-learning tonight: **a plausible explanation that fits the symptom is not a measurement.** The cheap read-only probe existed the whole time; I reached for a story first.
